opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kimberly Dennis (employee ID E010) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E010.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted. Full-time employees max at write for systems they don't own. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E010 (Kimberly Dennis) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max at read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed), so recommend read for Source Code, not the requested admin.
reason: Kimberly Dennis (E010) requested admin access to Source Code. HR records show she is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted for her (admin requires the employee's role to own the system). Full-time employees max out at write for systems they don't own. Since the requested admin level is above the maximum of write, I grant the maximum: write. (Note: the Security agent listed her as a contractor with basic training; however, under either classification admin is not permitted, and per the authoritative HR employment record the maximum is write.)
